# The functions

Every function a formula can call, by what it is for. The list is written
from the engine's own catalogue, so it has every function and no other.

A name is written in capitals and matches in any case. An argument in
square brackets may be left out, and `...` means it may be repeated.
A function marked **not built yet** is part of the language and is
refused by this version of the engine.

## Where a function may stand

Each function is of one kind, which decides where it may be used.

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| pure | A function of its arguments only. Allowed everywhere. |
| context | Reads the caller's context: the user, the clock, the document's state and id. Not allowed in auto formulas. |
| lookup | Reads one value from a table or stack. In auto formulas only against explicit tables. |
| query | Reads rows from a table or stack. Not allowed in auto formulas. |
| secret | Reads a secret the host program supplies for a connection. Allowed only in the request of an action definition. |

An auto formula is the formula of a computed variable that the engine
works out again whenever a value it reads changes.

## Logic

Conditions, and what to answer when something is missing or fails.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `IF(condition, then, else)` | pure | The second argument when the condition is TRUE, else the third. Only the chosen branch is evaluated. IF c THEN a ELSE b is the same expression. |
| `AND(condition[, condition, ...])` | pure | TRUE when every condition is TRUE, evaluated left to right and stopping at the first FALSE. Also the operator a AND b. |
| `OR(condition[, condition, ...])` | pure | TRUE when any condition is TRUE, evaluated left to right and stopping at the first TRUE. Also the operator a OR b. |
| `NOT(condition)` | pure | The opposite of the condition. Also the operator NOT a. |
| `ISBLANK(value)` | pure | TRUE only for a blank, never for a stored 0 or an empty text. |
| `ISNOTBLANK(value)` | pure | TRUE for anything but a blank. |
| `IFERROR(value, fallback)` | pure | The value, or the fallback when evaluating the value stops with an error. The fallback must have the value's type or be blank. |

## Numbers

Arithmetic on numbers as a spreadsheet keeps them.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `ROUND(number[, digits[, method]])` | pure | Rounds to the given decimal places by the method: half_up (the default, a half away from zero), half_even, down (toward zero), up (away from zero), floor or ceiling, written in the formula. Negative digits round to tens, hundreds and so on. On an exact value the digits are written in the formula and give the result's scale; the result keeps the kind, decimal or money. |
| `FLOOR(number[, digits])` | pure | Rounds down, toward minus infinity, at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale. |
| `CEILING(number[, digits])` | pure | Rounds up, toward plus infinity, at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale. Also written `CEIL`. |
| `TRUNC(number[, digits])` | pure | Cuts the number toward zero at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale. |
| `ABS(number)` | pure | The magnitude of the number. An exact value keeps its kind and scale. |
| `SIGN(number)` | pure | -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of the number; an int for an exact value. |
| `MIN(value[, value, ...])` | pure | The smallest of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. The values are of one family: all numbers, or all exact, at the largest scale, money of one currency. |
| `MAX(value[, value, ...])` | pure | The largest of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. The values are of one family, as for MIN. |
| `SUM(value[, value, ...])` | pure | The sum of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Exact values add exactly at the largest scale, money of one currency. |
| `AVERAGE(value[, value, ...])` | pure | The mean of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. Exact values divide at the largest scale plus four, half away from zero. |
| `COUNT(value[, value, ...])` | pure | How many of the values and array elements given are not blank. COUNT of a rows value is its number of rows. |
| `POWER(number, power)` | pure | The number raised to the power. The same as the ^ operator. |
| `SQRT(number)` | pure | The square root. A negative number is the error not_a_number. |
| `EXP(number)` | pure | e raised to the number. |
| `LN(number)` | pure | The natural logarithm. Zero or a negative number is the error not_a_number. |
| `LOG(number[, base])` | pure | The logarithm in the given base, 10 when omitted. A number at or below zero, or a base at or below zero or equal to 1, is the error not_a_number. |
| `MOD(number, divisor)` | pure | The remainder, with the sign of the divisor as in Excel. A zero divisor is the error div_by_zero. Exact values give an exact remainder at the larger scale. |

## Exact numbers and money

Amounts that must come out to the cent.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `DECIMAL(value, places[, method])` | pure | The value as an exact decimal with the given places, written in the formula, rounded by the method as ROUND does, half_up when omitted. A number is rounded at the places; a decimal or money is rescaled, money losing its currency. Blank stays blank. |
| `NUMBER(value)` | pure | The nearest number to an exact value, for the functions that need a number such as POWER and SQRT. Blank stays blank. |
| `MONEY(amount, currency)` | pure | The amount as money in the currency, three upper-case letters such as "PLN"; anything else is the error bad_text. A number literal amount is read exactly. A blank amount is blank. |
| `MONEYVALUE(text, places)` | pure | The money written as an amount, a space and a currency, such as "12.30 PLN", at the given places, written in the formula. Empty text is blank; a malformed text is the error bad_text; an amount with more places than asked is the error inexact. |
| `DECIMALVALUE(text, places)` | pure | The exact number written in the text, at the given places, written in the formula. Empty text is blank; a malformed text is the error bad_text; more places than asked is the error inexact; more than 18 digits is the error overflow. |
| `AMOUNT(money)` | pure | The amount of a money as a decimal at the same scale. Blank for a blank money. |
| `CURRENCY(money)` | pure | The currency code of a money. Blank for a blank money. |

## Text

Building, cutting and searching text.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `LEFT(text, count)` | pure | The first count characters, the whole text when the count is longer. A negative count is the error out_of_range. |
| `RIGHT(text, count)` | pure | The last count characters, the whole text when the count is longer. A negative count is the error out_of_range. |
| `MID(text, position[, length])` | pure | The characters from the 1-based position, to the end when the length is omitted or runs past it. A position below 1 or a negative length is the error out_of_range. |
| `LEN(text)` | pure | The number of characters, counted as Unicode code points. |
| `TRIM(text)` | pure | The text without leading and trailing spaces and with runs of inner spaces collapsed to one, as in Excel. |
| `UPPER(text)` | pure | The text in upper case, Unicode simple case mapping. |
| `LOWER(text)` | pure | The text in lower case, Unicode simple case mapping. |
| `PROPER(text)` | pure | The first letter of every word in upper case and the rest in lower case. |
| `URLENCODE(text)` | pure | The text made safe for a URL: letters, digits and - . _ ~ stay, and every other character becomes its UTF-8 bytes as %XX with upper-case hex digits, so a space is %20. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `REPLACE(text, position, length, new_text)` | pure | The text with length characters from the 1-based position replaced by the new text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `SUBSTITUTE(text, old_text, new_text)` | pure | The text with every occurrence of the old text replaced by the new text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `CONCAT(text[, text, ...])` | pure | The arguments joined into one text, each rendered as TEXT does. The same as the & operator. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `REPEAT(text, count)` | pure | The text repeated count times. A negative count, or a result longer than the text limit, is the error out_of_range. |
| `FINDFIRST(search, text)` | pure | The 1-based position of the first occurrence of the search text, case-sensitive, or 0 when absent. Also written `FIND`. |
| `FINDLAST(search, text)` | pure | The 1-based position of the last occurrence of the search text, case-sensitive, or 0 when absent. |
| `PAD(text, width[, fill])` | pure | The text padded on the left with the fill character, a space when omitted, up to the width. Longer text is returned unchanged. A width above the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `REGEXREPLACE(text, pattern, replacement)` | pure | The text with every match of the RE2 pattern replaced by the replacement, taken literally: no backreferences. An invalid pattern is rejected at definition time when it is a literal; an invalid pattern built at run time is the error bad_text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range. |
| `TEXT(value)` | pure | The value as text: numbers with 15 significant digits and no trailing zeros, exact values with every digit of their scale, money as the amount, a space and the currency, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, TRUE and FALSE, refs as Class:id, blank as empty text. |
| `VALUE(text)` | pure | The number written in the text: optional sign, digits, fraction and exponent, with a dot as the decimal point. Empty text is blank; anything else is the error bad_text. |

## Dates and times

Calendar days and moments.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `DATE(year, month, day)` | pure | The calendar day given. Fractions are truncated and overflow carries: month 14 is February of the next year, day 0 is the last day of the month before. |
| `DATEVALUE(text)` | pure | The calendar day written as YYYY-MM-DD. Empty text is blank; anything else, a time of day included, is the error bad_text. |
| `DATETIMEVALUE(text)` | pure | The instant written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DD, read as UTC. Empty text is blank; anything else is the error bad_text. |
| `DATEOF(datetime)` | pure | The calendar day of an instant, in UTC. Blank for a blank datetime. |
| `DATETIME(date)` | pure | Midnight UTC of a calendar day. Blank for a blank date. |
| `YEAR(date)` | pure | The year of the date or instant. Blank for a blank. |
| `MONTH(date)` | pure | The month of the date or instant, 1 to 12. Blank for a blank. |
| `DAY(date)` | pure | The day of the month of the date or instant. Blank for a blank. |
| `QUARTER(date)` | pure | The quarter of the date or instant, 1 to 4. Blank for a blank. |
| `DAYS(end_date, start_date)` | pure | Calendar days from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, an instant taken at its UTC midnight first. Blank when either is blank. |
| `DAYSBETWEEN(start_date, end_date)` | pure | Calendar day boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank. |
| `MONTHSBETWEEN(start_date, end_date)` | pure | Calendar month boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank. |
| `YEARSBETWEEN(start_date, end_date)` | pure | Calendar year boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank. |
| `ADDDAYS(date, days)` | pure | The date or instant moved by the given number of days: whole days on a date, fractions moving the time of day on a datetime. Blank for a blank. |
| `ADDMONTHS(date, months)` | pure | The date or instant moved by whole months, keeping the day of month and the time of day and clamping to the last day of a shorter month. Blank for a blank. |
| `ADDYEARS(date, years)` | pure | The date or instant moved by whole years, clamping 29 February to 28 February in a common year. Blank for a blank. |

## Lists, objects and rows

Values that hold several values.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `INDEX(array, position)` | pure | The element at the 1-based position. A position outside the array is the error out_of_range. **Not built yet.** |
| `FILTER(values, mask)` | pure | The elements or rows where the mask, an array of bool of the same length, is TRUE. **Not built yet.** |
| `FIRST(array)` | pure | The first element, or blank for an empty array. **Not built yet.** |
| `LAST(array)` | pure | The last element, or blank for an empty array. **Not built yet.** |
| `CONTAINS(array, value)` | pure | TRUE when an element equals the value, compared as the = operator does. **Not built yet.** |
| `JOIN(array, separator)` | pure | The elements rendered as TEXT does and joined with the separator, blanks skipped. **Not built yet.** |
| `JSONVALUE(json, path)` | pure | One value read from a json value at a dotted path such as address.city or items.0.sku, as text: numbers as TEXT renders them, booleans as TRUE and FALSE. Blank when the path is absent or null; an object or array at the path is the error bad_text. Convert with VALUE or DATEVALUE. |

## The caller, the clock and the document

Who is calling, what time it is, and what the engine keeps about the document: its state, who made it, when it entered a state.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `NOW()` | context | The current instant in UTC, to the second. |
| `TODAY()` | context | The current calendar day in UTC. |
| `USER()` | context | The id of the user on whose behalf the formula runs. Blank for a system recompute. |
| `INGROUP(group)` | context | TRUE when the current user is a member of the named group. |
| `USERKIND()` | context | What the current user is: person, agent or service. Blank when the host program does not say. |
| `ACTINGFOR()` | context | The id of whoever the current user acts for. Blank when it acts for itself. |
| `STATE()` | context | The state of the document the formula runs over. Blank for a class without states. |
| `ID()` | context | The id of the document the formula runs over. Blank when there is no document. |
| `CREATEDAT()` | context | The instant the document the formula runs over was created. Blank when there is no document. |
| `CREATEDBY()` | context | The id of the user whose command created the document. Blank when the command named nobody. |
| `UPDATEDAT()` | context | The instant the current version of the document was made. |
| `UPDATEDBY()` | context | The id of the user whose command made the current version of the document. Blank when the command named nobody. |
| `ENTEREDAT()` | context | The instant the document entered the state it is in. A transition back into the same state is an entry too. Blank for a class without states. |
| `ENTEREDBY()` | context | The id of the user whose command moved the document into the state it is in. Blank when the command named nobody. |
| `ENTEREDFROM()` | context | The state the document was in before the one it is in: that same state after a transition back into it, blank while it is in the state it was created in. |
| `VERSION()` | context | The version of the document the formula runs over. Blank when there is no document. |
| `FIRSTENTERED(state)` | context | The instant the document first entered the state. Blank when it never did. |
| `FIRSTENTEREDBY(state)` | context | The id of the user whose command first moved the document into the state. Blank when it never entered it, and when the command named nobody. |
| `LASTENTERED(state)` | context | The instant the document last entered the state, a transition back into it counted. Blank when it never did. |
| `LASTENTEREDBY(state)` | context | The id of the user whose command last moved the document into the state. Blank when it never entered it, and when the command named nobody. |
| `FIRSTLEFT(state)` | context | The instant the document first left the state. Blank when it never left it. |
| `FIRSTLEFTBY(state)` | context | The id of the user whose command first moved the document out of the state. Blank when it never left it, and when the command named nobody. |
| `LASTLEFT(state)` | context | The instant the document last left the state; for a document that is in the state, the time before. Blank when it never left it. |
| `LASTLEFTBY(state)` | context | The id of the user whose command last moved the document out of the state. Blank when it never left it, and when the command named nobody. |
| `ENTRIES(state)` | context | How many times the document entered the state, a transition back into it counted. 0 when it never did, blank when there is no document. |
| `DAYSIN(state)` | context | The days the document has spent in the state in all, with fractions, up to now when it is there. 0 when it never was, blank when there is no document. |
| `FIRSTEDITOR(state)` | context | The id of the first user who created the document in the state or changed it there. Moving it in or out is not a change. Blank when nobody did. |
| `LASTEDITOR(state)` | context | The id of the last user who created the document in the state or changed it there. Moving it in or out is not a change. Blank when nobody did. |
| `SECRET(name)` | secret | The secret of that name, which the connection of an action definition declares and the host program supplies when the request is sent. The name is a text literal. Only the request of an action definition may use it; the engine stores no secret. |

## Tables and other documents

Values looked up outside the document.

| Function | Kind | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `LOOKUP(source, column, condition)` | lookup | One column of the first row of the source, in key order, that matches the condition; blank when none does. In place of the column, COUNT, SUM, MIN or MAX over one expression of the source's columns answers for every matching row. Inside, bare names are the source's columns and THIS.name reaches the document. |
| `QUERY(source, columns[, condition[, sort[, groupby[, limit]]]])` | query | The rows of the source matching the condition, with the given columns, which may be aggregates, in the given sort, grouped by the given columns, at most limit rows (1,000 by default, 10,000 at most). **Not built yet.** |
